Δ=0 forces at most one effective node, possibly zero. The complete seven-case marginal table reconstructs all possibilities; pair choices for equal coefficients differ in cross moment by c(z1−z2)(w1−w2)≠0; if an entire marginal cancels, its common node is H/X1 or H/Y1 with guaranteed nonzero denominator. All output candidates are tested against eight exact moment equations and torus constraints. 700 random plus 5355 structured finite configurations passed supplementary checker; finite checks are not used as a proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge distinction is constructive: the 2021 paper Theorem 9/Corollary 10 proves uniqueness of the eight-index hyperbolic cross but explicitly does not give a reconstruction algorithm from it; Theorem 11 gives a larger 12-index constructive set at N=d=2. The branchwise inversion here uses only eight indices and covers cancelling/merged marginals by one mixed moment. Sauer symbolic Prony and Cuyt-Lee projection algorithms require other sample patterns or adaptive extra samples. Targeted published-finding corpus queries found no equivalent fixed-eight, collision-complete reconstruction theorem; absence of hits alone cannot certify priority.

value.rationale: A natural gap is stated explicitly in the 2021 primary literature: the sharp O(N log^(d-1) N) hyperbolic-cross uniqueness proof does not construct an inverse, and its constructive replacement enlarges the sample set. In the first nontrivial N=d=2 case, this theorem supplies exact reconstruction at the original eight fixed frequencies for all complex amplitudes and non-generic marginal cancellations, with a precise diagnostic of why one mixed sample is essential. This is an actionable structured inverse-problem benchmark, not merely an ordinary rephrasing of the known injectivity statement.
